record.paper_title: Variants of the focusing NLS equation. Derivation, justification and open problems related to filamentation
record.original_question:
Fix d in {2, 3}, let v_0 in H^1(R^d) be initial data for the cubic focusing NLS that produce a finite-time blow-up solution v at time T > 0, and let v_epsilon be the solution of the regularized equation

 i partial_t v + Delta v + (1 + f(epsilon^r |v|^2)) |v|^2 v = 0

with the same initial data. What is the limiting behavior of v_epsilon(t) as epsilon tends to 0 for times t > T, that is, after the blow-up time of the unregularized cubic NLS has already passed?

evidence.quote: (51) i∂tv + ∆v + (1 + f(ε^r|v|^2))|v|^2v = 0, t > 0, x ∈ R^d, where the dimension is d = 2 in the case of no GVD, and d = 3 in the case of anomalous GVD.
An interesting question is the understanding of the limit of v_epsilon(t) as epsilon -> 0 for t > T .

Open Problem 2. Let v0 in H1(Rd), d = 2, 3 be leading to a finite time blow-up solution v at time T > 0 to the cubic NLS (1). Consider the solution v_epsilon of (51) with the same initial data v0. Describe the behavior of v_epsilon(t) as epsilon -> 0 for t > T .

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $d \in \{2,3\}$ and consider the cubic focusing nonlinear Schrödinger equation
$$
i\partial_t v + \Delta v + |v|^2 v = 0, \qquad t > 0,\ x \in \mathbb{R}^d, \qquad v(0,\cdot) = v_0 \in H^1(\mathbb{R}^d),
$$
and assume that $v_0$ is chosen so that the corresponding solution $v$ blows up in $H^1(\mathbb{R}^d)$ at some finite time $T > 0$ (such initial data exist in both dimensions $d=2$ and $d=3$).

Fix a real number $r > 0$ and a smooth bounded function $f:[0,\infty) \to \mathbb{R}$ with $f(0)=0$ that saturates the cubic nonlinearity (so that the regularized nonlinearity $(1+f(\varepsilon^r |v|^2))|v|^2 v$ remains bounded enough to yield global-in-time solutions for every $\varepsilon > 0$). For each $\varepsilon > 0$, let $v_\varepsilon$ denote the global solution of the regularized equation
$$
i\partial_t v_\varepsilon + \Delta v_\varepsilon + \bigl(1 + f(\varepsilon^r |v_\varepsilon|^2)\bigr)|v_\varepsilon|^2 v_\varepsilon = 0, \qquad v_\varepsilon(0,\cdot) = v_0.
$$

It is known that on $[0,T)$, $v_\varepsilon \to v$ in a suitable sense as $\varepsilon \to 0$. Describe rigorously the limiting behavior of $v_\varepsilon(t,\cdot)$ as $\varepsilon \to 0$ for times $t > T$, i.e., past the blow-up time of the unregularized cubic NLS.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem is posed as an open question regarding the post-blow-up limit of saturated regularizations of the focusing cubic NLS in dimensions 2 and 3. Recent literature on saturated NLS variants and filamentation discusses regularization arresting blow-up but does not provide a rigorous description of the $\varepsilon \to 0$ limit beyond the blow-up time; no resolution was located.

status_evidence.title: Variants of the focusing NLS equation (arXiv)
status_evidence.snippet: Open problems related to filamentation, including the limit of regularized solutions past blow-up.
status_evidence.claim: The post-blow-up epsilon-to-zero limit is stated as an open problem.

status_evidence.title: On blowup solution in NLS equation under dispersion or nonlinearity management
status_evidence.snippet: Recent work on blow-up in NLS variants does not address rigorous post-blow-up limits of saturated regularizations.
status_evidence.claim: No rigorous resolution of the post-blow-up limit appears in recent NLS blow-up literature.

status_evidence.title: Filamentation patterns in Kerr media vs. nonlinear saturation
status_evidence.snippet: Saturating nonlinearities arrest blow-up and favor multi-filamentation, but the analysis is non-rigorous/physical.
status_evidence.claim: Saturation arrests blow-up but the post-blow-up limit is not rigorously characterized.
